svg.title: Why U, τ+5 copies of V and τ+6 copies of W cannot build an a×b×c frame
svg.desc: Here τ = a+b+c-6. Only U, V and W can be targets. Target U has two corner types that only U supplies, but there is one U. Targets V and W each have seven private corner types and one private edge type per axis, so τ+7 positions need a cube from a pool of only τ+6.

g.text: τ = a+b+c−6 counts the noncorner positions on one edge in each direction. Faded corners also occur outside the pool.
Only U, V and W can be targets. For a+b+c = 8 there are sixteen cubes, so 2×2×4 and 2×3×3 frames need seventeen.
